note: UK wall build-ups. Thicknesses are millimetres, listed from the outside in. `reviewed: true` means a person has signed the entry off; everything here is a draft from published UK practice and must be checked before anyone builds from it. Performance fields are present and deliberately empty: this extension does not compute or claim a U-value.

walls.source: Draft: the filled masonry cavity wall UK housebuilding has built since the Part L 2013 uplift — 102 mm brick, a fully filled cavity, 100 mm block. To be checked against a current NHBC detail before it is reviewed.
Draft: the same cavity with 125 mm of fill, the thickness most new-build plots are detailed with after the 2022 uplift. Verify the fill and the block together, not each alone.
Draft: a deep-filled cavity, used where the wall has to reach a tighter target than 125 mm of fill manages — and where the cavity stays wide enough to be built cleanly.
Draft: the pre-2013 cavity, which is what most of the existing housing stock actually is. Useful when modelling a building that stands, not one that is going up.
Draft: external wall insulation on a 140 mm block inner leaf, finished with a thin render. The common answer where the outer skin is not brick.
Draft: retrofit insulation over a solid 215 mm brick wall — the standard upgrade for pre-1930 housing. The wall it covers is 215 mm of brick, which is one brick length and not a guess.
Draft: a single-leaf rendered block wall, as built for garages, extensions and much of the inter-war stock. No cavity, so no insulation — this is a wall to model as it is, not as it should be.

name.en-GB: Timber frame with brick outer leaf

walls.source: Draft: the timber-frame wall that carries a masonry outer leaf — the Scottish housebuilder's standard, and increasingly used elsewhere.
walls.note: The 140 mm zone is the stud, counted as insulation: its mass is the insulation's, not the frame's. A vapour barrier is thinner than a skin may be, so it is part of the build-up and not a layer here.

walls.source: Draft: a ventilated timber-clad frame — cladding, a drained cavity, sheathing, the stud zone and a plasterboard lining.
walls.note: As above: the stud zone is counted as insulation, so the frame's mass is missing from the take-off.

walls.source: Draft: the infill panel between the columns of a concrete frame — an outer block leaf, a filled cavity and an inner block leaf. The frame itself is not part of this wall.
Draft: a 100 mm block partition, the default non-loadbearing wall in UK domestic work.
Draft: a 140 mm block wall — a partition that also carries, or one that has to meet a fire or acoustic line a 100 mm cannot.
Draft: a solid 215 mm block separating wall between dwellings. What it has to meet acoustically and in fire is a requirement, not a property of this stack.
Draft: two block leaves with a 50 mm cavity between them — the other way a separating wall is built, and the one that leaves room for a service zone.
Draft: the timber stud partition of domestic work — 89 mm studs and a plasterboard each side.
walls.note: The 89 mm zone is the stud, counted as timber: an insulated stud partition is a different wall (see the acoustic one).

walls.source: Draft: a stud partition with the cavity filled — the party-wall and bedroom-wall detail. The studs are not modelled, so the 75 mm zone is counted as insulation.
walls.note: Counted as insulation, so the frame's mass is missing; the acoustic performance is a matter for the specification, not for this stack.

name.en-GB: Stud partition with a service void 89-25

walls.source: Draft: a stud partition with a 25 mm service zone on one side, so the pipes do not have to be buried in the wall they run through.
Draft: a half-brick internal wall, which is what a great deal of older housing actually has where a modern drawing would show block.
Draft: a 200 mm concrete core or flank wall, the structure around which the rest of the building is planned.
Draft: a block wall with a plasterboard lining on one face — how a block wall usually ends up looking, and how its thickness usually gets quoted.
